newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-TRACY WINS FIRST INDY CAR POLE OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-TRACY WINS FIRST INDY CAR POLE OF YEAR.

text.p: Canadian Paul Tracy, seeking to end his longest winless streak, clinched his first pole position of the season on Saturday for Sunday's CART Indy car race, but said the hardest part was still to come.
Driving a Penske Mercedes-Benz, Tracy set a record 18.831 seconds (191.174 mph) ahead of Sunday's 225 mile race to become the first repeat pole winner at the one mile oval.

"Starting from the pole doesn't mean a thing," said Tracy, seeking his first victory since May 1995. "This is going to be a difficult race, a longer race," he added. Twenty five laps were added to last year's 200 miler.
Nazareth native Michael Andretti, winner of the opening round at Homestead, Florida, was second fastest in a Swift Ford at 19.163 after suffering a loss of power.
"The popoff valve was stuck open the whole time so we lost a lot of speed right there. So it was really disappointing," said Andretti.
Rookie Patrick Carpentier of Canada, third in practice on Friday, held onto that position with a time of 19.204 in a Reynard Mercedes-Benz.
Brazilian Gil de Ferran, pole winner of the last CART race, at Long Beach, was fourth fastest in a Reynard Honda at 19.265 seconds.
Italy's Alessandro Zanardi's record 11 front row starts came to an end as he went out on a recently cleaned track and qualified 21st in a Reynard Honda.
A victory here for Tracy is crucial to end the longest winless streak, at 20, for the once vaunted Penske Racing Team.

"This is my longest dry period," said Tracy after his tenth career pole. "Just because you're fast in every practice and win the pole doesn't mean you'll win the race. Everything has to go near as perfect as it can."
Twenty-six cars are scheduled to start Sunday's race, the fourth in the 17 race series.
